items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Sacha found out that the Mayor who would perform the ritual was a buddy from the war. They started a long conversation about the days they had passed together in the Resistance.

ctx.x: Louis Lamy, the owner of the bus we had hired, came to see us about lunch time, then somebody else and about 4 a.m. "Bish" came in our hotel room and started to tell us some story. We were nervous and finally had to push him our of the room, telling him: "Bish, we have got to get dressed, because we are going to get married...." If we would not have been in such a hurry, it would have been comic to see his face!

We arrived at the Town Hall just in time, but realized that we had forgotten about hiring a photographer. Maurice said he was going to try to find one. We went upstairs and Sacha found out that the Mayor who would perform the ritual was a buddy from the war. They started a long conversation about the days they had passed together in the Resistance. Maurice was coming in, time to time, to say he had no luck in finding a photographer.

Finally, the ceremony began without a photographer. At one time, the Mayor said something which I did not understand because my French was no hell. There was a silence and then I decided to say 'oui'(wee in French) and I hit the right note. I was expecting Sacha to give me a hint, as we do in the States, when I was to say 'oui', but that didn't happen so I played it by ear and came out right at the coda.
